title: The Classic American Starter Board
seo_title: Classic Charcuterie Board for Beginners: Shopping List & Plan for 8–12
description: A first charcuterie board anyone can build: cheddar, salami, grapes, pickles and honey. What to buy, why it works and a 20-minute plan for 8–12 people.
hook: The board to make first. Supermarket ingredients, no hunting, and every bite still has something sweet, something sharp and something salty to push against.
why: Three cheeses that cover the range most guests already like: a sharp one, a mild melty one, and a soft spread. Three salamis that are all salt and fat, which is exactly why the rest of the board is built to cut through them.

Apple and grapes bring the acid and cold sweetness that make cheddar taste brighter. Dill pickles and whole-grain mustard do the same job for the meats: vinegar slices through fat, so each bite of salami tastes clean instead of heavy. Honey goes next to the cheddar, where sweet against sharp is the whole point.

timeline.what: Take the cheeses and meats out of the fridge.
Slice the cheddar and apple; fill the small bowls.
Place the cheeses first; spoon in the mustard and honey.
Fan the meats, then add fruit, crackers and almonds.
Guests arrive. Refill crackers every 20 minutes.

faq.q: How many people does this board serve?
faq.a: 8 to 12 people as an appetizer, on a 16–20 inch board.
Slice the hard cheese and meats up to a day ahead and keep them wrapped. Cut the apple and put out the crackers just before serving so nothing goes soft or brown.

faq.q: What's the easiest swap if someone can't have pork?
faq.a: Swap the three pork salamis for beef summer sausage and thin-sliced smoked turkey.
